He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Gonzaga Bulldogs men's basketball|Gonzaga Bulldogs]]. Tillie joined [[Gonzaga Bulldogs men's basketball|Gonzaga University]] beginning in the 2016–17 season.{{cite web|title=French forward Killian Tillie commits to Gonzaga|url=http://www.spokesman.com/stories/2015/aug/29/french-forward-killian-tillie-commits-gonzaga/|date=August 29, 2015}} ==Youth career== Tillie played basketball and volleyball until the age of 14, before choosing to focus on basketball. He started his basketball career in the youth setup at Cagnes Basket, when he was six years of age. He then moved to Stade Laurentin Basket, before joining the youth academy of [[Olympique Antibes|Olympique d'Antibes]] in 2013.{{Cite web|title = Killian Tillie : nouvelle pépite du basket français|url = http://sportsspirit.org/2014/11/29/killian-tillie-nouvelle-pepite-du-basket-francais/|website = SportsSpirit|access-date = February 6, 2016|last = umdf|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20160206232825/http://sportsspirit.org/2014/11/29/killian-tillie-nouvelle-pepite-du-basket-francais/|archive-date = February 6, 2016|url-status = dead}} Prior to the 2014–15 season, he joined the INSEP academy.{{Cite web|title = Basket-Ball : un Tillie en cache toujours un autre|url = http://www.paris-normandie.fr/detail_sport/articles/1246712/tiens-encore-un-tillie-#.VrY1E8eJR8c|website = www.paris-normandie.fr|access-date = February 6, 2016}} ===Recruiting=== {{quote box|width=23em|align=right|quote="Killian is a dynamic athlete that will end up being a very good faceup-type four. Once we get him in the weight room and work on his strength, he’ll be a very good player at the highest level."|source=— [[Mark Few]], Gonzaga Head Coach.{{cite web|title=Gonzaga MBB Inks Four to NLI in Early Signing Period|url=http://www.gozags.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/112015aaa.html|date=November 20, 2015|access-date=February 23, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160107064743/http://www.gozags.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/112015aaa.html|archive-date=January 7, 2016|url-status=dead}}}} {{quote box|width=23em|align=right|quote="We expect him to contribute right away, if his health is under control with some knee issues. He is one of those really interesting guys. He has incredible instincts. It's probably hard to pinpoint his strengths, but he doesn’t really have a weakness either. He has tremendous upside, and we think his potential is off the charts."|source=— [[Tommy Lloyd]], Gonzaga Associate Head Coach.{{cite web|title=Next international wave will set up Zags for a while, says GU's Lloyd|url=http://www.heinnews.com/basketball/nba/next-international-wave-will-set-up-zags-for-a-while-says-gus-lloyd/|date=December 9, 2015}}}} In January 2015, Tillie was highlighted by [[ESPN]] among five of the best international players in the 2015 and 2016 classes with aspirations to play college basketball. He was drawing major interest from California at the time, and scouts were impressed with his terrific offensive rebounding, athleticism and high motor.{{cite web|title=The next wave of international prospects|url=https://insider.espn.com/blog/ncbrecruiting/on-the-trail/insider/post?id=12808|date=January 31, 2015}} In August 2015, Tillie traveled to the United States and took official visits to Georgia Tech, Utah, and Gonzaga.{{cite web|title=Top French forward, 6-8 Killian Tillie, is on his visit to Georgia Tech, followed by trips to Utah and Gonzaga. Brother of former Ute, Kim.|url=https://twitter.com/franfraschilla/status/633366881328455680|date=August 17, 2015}} Less than a week after his trip to Spokane, he verbally to committed to play college basketball at [[Gonzaga Bulldogs men's basketball|Gonzaga University]], citing the Zags' "success with international players and because of the people that love basketball there." He signed with the Zags in the early signing period in November 2015. {{College athlete recruit start|40=no|collapse=no|year=2016}} {{College athlete recruit entry | recruit = Killian Tillie | web|url=http://www.gozags.com/sports/m-baskbl/stats/2016-2017/gonmbbex.html|title=West Georgia vs Gonzaga|date=November 5, 2016|website=gozags.com|publisher=Gonzaga University|access-date=November 12, 2016}} As a freshman during the 2016–17 season, Tillie appeared in 33 games, averaging 4.2 points and 3.2 rebounds in 12.3 minutes.{{Cite web|url=http://www.gozags.com/sports/m-baskbl/stats/2016-2017/teamcume.html#TEAM.IND|title=Season Box Score|website=gozags.com|access-date=April 18, 2017}} He saw 14 minutes of action in the [[2017 NCAA Division I Men's Basketball Championship Game|NCAA championship game]] against [[North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball|North Carolina]], pulling down nine rebounds and scoring one point.{{Cite web|url=http://www.gozags.com/sports/m-baskbl/stats/2016-2017/gonmbb39.html|title=Gonzaga vs North Carolina (04/03/17 at Univ of Phoenix Stadium, Glendale, AZ), Official Basketball Box Score|website=gozags.com|access-date=April 18, 2017}} As a sophomore in 2017–18, Tillie was Gonzaga's second leading scorer, averaging 12.9 points in 26.2 minutes per game to go along with 5.9 rebounds and 1 blocked shot per contest.{{Cite web|url=http://www.gozags.com/sports/m-baskbl/stats/2017-2018/teamcume.html#TEAM.IND|title=2017-18 Gonzaga Men's Basketball Season Box Score|website=gozags.com|access-date=March 27, 2018}} Coming into his junior season, Tillie was named to the Preseason All-WCC Team.{{Cite web|url=https://wccsports.com/news/2018/10/18/mens-basketball-wcc-unveils-2018-19-preseason-poll-all-wcc-team.aspx|title=Gonzaga picked to Win 2018-19 Men's Basketball Championship|work=[[West Coast Conference]]|date=October 18, 2018|access-date=October 18, 2018}} On October 30, 2018, it was announced that Tillie was to miss approximately eight weeks with a stress fracture on his ankle.{{cite news |last1=Johnson |first1=Raphielle |title=Stress fracture to sideline Gonzaga C Killian Tillie eight weeks |url=https://collegebasketball.nbcsports.com/2018/10/30/stress-fracture-to-sideline-gonzaga-c-killian-tillie-eight-weeks/ |access-date=October 30, 2018 |work=[[NBC Sports]] |date=October 30, 2018}} Tillie missed the beginning of his senior season recovering from a knee injury. He returned to the lineup on November 19, 2019, finishing with 15 points and eight rebounds as Gonzaga held off [[UT Arlington Mavericks men's basketball|Texas-Arlington]] 72–66.{{cite news |title=Woolridge leads No. 8 Gonzaga over Texas-Arlington 72–66 |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401174720 |access-date=November 20, 2019 |work=[[ESPN]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=November 19, 2019}} On January 30, 2020, Tillie left a game against [[Santa Clara Broncos men's basketball|Santa Clara]] in the first half after suffering an ankle injury.{{cite news |last1=Meehan |first1=Jim |title=Gonzaga forward Killian Tillie exits Santa Clara game with first-half ankle injury |url=https://www.spokesman.com/stories/2020/jan/30/gonzaga-forward-killian-tillie-exits-santa-clara-g/ |access-date=January 31, 2020 |work=[[The Spokesman-Review]] |date=January 30, 2020}} At the conclusion of the regular season, Tillie was named to the First Team All-WCC.{{cite press release|url=https://wccsports.com/news/2020/3/3/wcc-announces-2019-20-mens-basketball-all-conference-team-mbb.aspx |title=WCC Announces 2019-20 Men's Basketball All-Conference Team |publisher=West Coast Conference |date=March 3, 2020 |access-date=March 3, 2020}} He averaged 13.6 points and 5.0 rebounds per game as a senior.{{cite news |last1=Meehan |first1=Jim |title=Sources: Former Gonzaga forward Killian Tillie signing two-way deal with Memphis after going undrafted |url=https://www.spokesman.com/stories/2020/nov/18/former-gonzaga-forward-killian-tillie-goes-undraft/ |access-date=November 19, 2020 |work=[[The Spokesman-Review]] |date=November 18, 2020}} ==Professional career== ===Memphis Grizzlies (2020–2022)=== After going undrafted in the [[2020 NBA draft]], Tillie signed a two-way contract with the [[Memphis Grizzlies]] on 24 November 2020.{{cite web|title=Grizzlies sign Killian Tillie and Sean McDermott to two-way contracts|url=https://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/grizzlies-sign-killian-tillie-and-sean-mcdermott-to-two-way-contracts-201124|website=NBA.com|date=24 November 2020|access-date=24 November 2020}} On 12 August 2021, Tillie signed a second two-way contract with the Grizzlies.{{cite web|title=Grizzlies sign Killian Tillie to two-way contract|url=https://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/grizzlies-sign-killian-tillie-to-two-way-contract-210812|website=NBA.com|date=12 August 2021|access-date=14 August 2021}} On 1 January 2022, he signed a two-year standard contract.{{cite web|title=Memphis Grizzlies sign forward Killian Tillie to a two-year contract, waive Sam Merrill|url=https://www.commercialappeal.com/story/sports/nba/grizzlies/2022/01/01/memphis-grizzlies-sign-forward-killian-tillie-two-year-contract-waive-sam-merrill/9069904002/|work=The Commercial Appeal|access-date=1 January 2022}} The Grizzlies waived Tillie on 15 October 2022, before the start of the 2022–23 season.{{cite web|first=Drew|last=Hill|title=Grizzlies waive Killian Tillie before start of season|url=https://dailymemphian.com/article/31595/memphis-grizzlies-waive-killian-tillie-before-start-of-season|work=Daily Memphian|date=15 October 2022|access-date=15 October (2024–present)=== On 21 August 2024, Tillie signed with [[Baloncesto Málaga|Unicaja]] of the [[Liga ACB]].{{cite web|title=Killian Tillie se incorpora al Unicaja|url=https://www.unicajabaloncesto.com/noticia/ver/id/236249/titulo/killian-tillie-se-incorpora-al-unicaja.html|website=UnicajaBaloncesto.com|date=21 August 2024|access-date=21 August 2024|language=Spanish}} ==National team career== Tillie helped the French Under-16 National Team win the [[2014 FIBA Europe Under-16 Championship]], averaging 14.3 points, 9.6 rebounds, 1.7 assists, 1.2 blocked shots and 1.2 steals a contest, while being recognized as [[2014 FIBA Europe Under-16 Championship#All-Tournament Team|the tournament's MVP]].{{Cite web|title = Tillie Towers Above The Competition {{!}} U16 Europe Championship Men - Division A|url = http://u16men.fibaeurope.com/en/coid_RZGz4WBjI0EEwGX6OT5LZ1.articleMode_on.html|website = u16men.fibaeurope.com|access-date = February 6, 2016|archive-date = May 9, 2015|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20150509194941/http://u16men.fibaeurope.com/en/coid_RZGz4WBjI0EEwGX6OT5LZ1.articleMode_on.html|url-status = dead}} He dropped in 25 points and grabbed 18 boards, in the title game, a 78–53 win over hosting Latvia.{{Cite web|url = http://www.fibaeurope.com/compID_YUjW-7-FJ%2CkK9s431Lyr41.season_2014.roundID_9771.gameID_10124-72-A-1.html|title = Boxscore Final Latvia - France|date = August 30, 2014|access-date = February 6, 2016|website = fibaeurope.com|publisher = FIBA Europe}} In the summer of 2015, Tillie competed in the [[FIBA 3x3 Under-18 World Championships]], where he teamed up with [[Bathiste Tchouaffe]], Jules Rambaut, and Timothe Vergiat and he represented France at the 2015 World Championship, in Debrecen, Hungary, where they finished in third place, with an 8–1 record. His team defeated USA, featuring fellow Gonzaga commit [[Zach Collins]], in the quarter-finals, before losing to Argentina in the semifinals, and thumping Spain in the third-place game.{{cite web|title=FIBA 3x3 Profile: Killian Tillie|url=http://www.3x3planet.com/en/PlayerProfile?playerFibaId=PLF14KUDVXWURFRA|access-date=April 4, 2016}}{{Dead link|date=June 2025 |bot=InternetArchiveBot 4.6 || 1.4 || .8 || .7 || 9.5 {{S-end}} ==Personal life== He is the son of [[Laurent Tillie]], a former professional volleyball player and coach of the [[France men's national volleyball team|French national team]], and Caroline Keulen-Tillie, a former professional volleyball player from the Netherlands. Killian's brothers are also professional athletes: [[Kim Tillie]] plays basketball and [[Kévin Tillie|Kevin Tillie]] plays volleyball.
